findings.claim: The new reportDiagnostic wrapper drops every diagnostic whose Location is not IsInSource. Diagnostics that were previously reported with Location.None, for example when a null location is passed, are now silently suppressed. A user type whose diagnostic lacks a source location, such as one using GetLocation helpers that return null, no longer gets that diagnostic. This is a behaviour change for same-assembly types, which are meant to "keep working as before".

receipt_plan.detail: Run the analyzer tests for MsgPack003/004/005/006/007/008/009 and others that report with GetLocation(...) helpers returning null on a source type. Check that no diagnostic previously reported is now missing. Compare the diagnostics from a build with base vs head over the existing analyzer test suite.

findings.claim: The filter does not fix the crash from the other unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` indexers the reporter named. Only the property-identifier site (now GetPropertyIdentifierLocation) and the two guarded contractAttr sites are fixed. Other paths in GetObjectInfo are unguarded for a metadata closed generic struct (e.g. around line 735), so the crash may remain. Also, for a metadata type the whole GetObjectInfo still runs and the resulting ObjectSerializationInfo is built, which may differ from the non-generic metadata case, where CollectCore returns early.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator/analyzer test with a two-compilation setup: a referenced-assembly `[MessagePackObject] struct Item<T>` with [Key] members, used as `Item<int>` in a MessagePackObject in the app. Assert there is no CS8785/AD0001 and that a GeneratedMessagePackResolver is produced. Also test with members lacking keys and with the init property.
